Cada token produce sus tres vectores mul: Each token produces its three vectors by multiplying its representation by three matrices that are learned: $\vec q = \vec x W_Q$, $\vec k = \vec x W_K$, $\vec v = \vec x W_V$. The same word does all three jobs as its turn comes: it asks when it is the one looking, and it offers key and value when it is being looked at.

Casi todo lo que hoy se usa con lenguaje: Almost everything used with language today — translating, summarising, answering, programming — is a stack of these blocks. And it is worth knowing one practical consequence of the formula: since each position is compared with all of them, the cost grows with the square of the text's length. Doubling the context quadruples attention's work. That is why large context windows are expensive, and why there is so much research into approximate versions that do not have to compute the whole matrix.

La atención se inventó en 2014 para trad: Attention was invented in 2014 for machine translation, as a patch to recurrent networks: Dzmitry Bahdanau, Kyunghyun Cho and Yoshua Bengio proposed letting the decoder look at all the encoder's states instead of a single summary. In 2017 a team at Google published Attention Is All You Need, whose thesis was the title's: removing the recurrence and leaving only attention, not only was no quality lost but it was gained, and besides it could be trained in parallel. That paper defines the architecture still used today.
La atención trata la entrada como un con: Attention treats the input as a set, not as a sequence: each weight depends only on the two vectors involved, not on where they are. Without adding the position, “the dog bites the man” and “the man bites the dog” would give the same thing.
La forma original fue sumar a cada token: The original way was to add to each token a vector depending only on its position, built with [[tr-funciones|sines and cosines]] of different frequencies.

Measured with $d = 32$, the pairs 5→8, 20→23 and 40→43 all three give exactly 0.7670. It is read from the inside out. $QK^t$ is all the dot products of each query with each key, in one go: row $i$, column $j$ is how well query $i$ fits key $j$.

The softmax turns each row into weights that add to one, and on multiplying by $V$ each position receives the weighted average of all the values. That is all: a weighted average whose weights are computed with dot products.
